title: GMAT Focus Data Insights Practice Test 14
instructions: Original exam-style practice test with answers and explanations.

questions.prompt:
Births and deaths per 1,000 people, in five countries:

Aldia: 14.2 births, 8.6 deaths
Bresk: 21 births, 16.4 deaths
Corva: 11.8 births, 9.1 deaths
Dunmar: 18.5 births, 12.2 deaths
Estone: 9.4 births, 10.7 deaths

Which country has the highest natural increase — births less deaths?
options: A. Aldia
B. Bresk
C. Corva
D. Estone
E. Dunmar
questions.explanation: Births minus deaths: Aldia +5.6, Bresk +4.6, Corva +2.7, Dunmar +6.3, Estone -1.3. Dunmar leads at 6.3 per 1,000. Bresk has much the highest birth rate at 21, but loses nearly as many people as it gains, so a high birth rate on its own settles nothing.

questions.prompt:
Imports and exports, in millions:

2020: imports 320, exports 290
2021: imports 355, exports 300
2022: imports 380, exports 296
2023: imports 402, exports 358
2024: imports 430, exports 415

In which year was the gap between imports and exports widest?
options: E. The gap was the same every year
questions.explanation: The gap year by year: 2020 30, 2021 55, 2022 84, 2023 44, 2024 15. 2022 is widest at 84. 2024 has the highest imports of any year but the narrowest gap, because exports had almost caught up by then.

questions.prompt:
An upgrade costs GBP 48,000.00 and is expected to save:

Year 1: GBP 11,000.00
Year 2: GBP 14,000.00
Year 3: GBP 16,000.00
Year 4: GBP 15,000.00
Year 5: GBP 13,000.00

In which year do the cumulative savings first cover the cost?
options: A. Year 2
B. Year 3
C. Year 5
D. Year 4
E. The savings never cover the cost
questions.explanation: Cumulative savings: Year 1 GBP 11,000.00, Year 2 GBP 25,000.00, Year 3 GBP 41,000.00, Year 4 GBP 56,000.00, Year 5 GBP 69,000.00. Year 3 ends GBP 7,000.00 short, so the cost is not covered until Year 4. The largest single year's saving falls in Year 3, which is a different question.

questions.prompt:
Seven readings, in order: 22, 24, 25, 25, 27, 29, 96

The reading of 96 is found to be an error and removed. Which statement about the effect is accurate?
options: A. The median falls along with the mean
B. The mode changes once the reading is removed
C. The mean falls sharply, the median and the mode are unchanged, and the range drops to under a tenth of its former size
D. The range is unchanged
E. The mean rises once the outlier is gone
questions.explanation: Before: mean 35.43, median 25, mode 25, range 74. After: mean 25.33, median 25, mode 25, range 7. One extreme value was carrying the mean roughly ten points above every reading around it, and stretching the range from 7 to 74. The median and the mode never noticed it, which is exactly why they are quoted when outliers are suspected.

questions.prompt:
Two accounts hold GBP 14,600.00 between them, and one holds GBP 3,200.00 more than the other.

Select the balance of each account.
options: C. GBP 7,300.00 in each
E. The two balances cannot be worked out
questions.explanation: Take the difference off the total first: GBP 14,600.00 − GBP 3,200.00 = GBP 11,400.00, which splits evenly into two lots of GBP 5,700.00. Adding the difference back to one of them gives GBP 8,900.00. Adding the whole GBP 3,200.00 to half the total gives GBP 10,500.00, which overshoots by half the difference.

questions.prompt:
An agent earns 3% commission on the first GBP 50,000.00 of sales and 5% on everything above that.

Select the commission on GBP 86,000.00 of sales AND the sales figure at which commission first reaches GBP 4,000.00.
questions.explanation: The first GBP 50,000.00 earns GBP 1,500.00, and the remaining GBP 36,000.00 earns GBP 1,800.00: GBP 3,300.00 in all. To reach GBP 4,000.00 the agent needs GBP 2,500.00 from the upper band, which at 5% takes GBP 50,000.00 of sales above GBP 50,000.00 — GBP 100,000.00 in total. Applying 3% to everything gives GBP 2,580.00 and ignores the upper band.

questions.prompt:
Two workers:

Worker One: GBP 18.40 an hour, 22 hours a week
Worker Two: GBP 14.90 an hour, 38 hours a week

Select the worker on the higher hourly rate AND the worker who earns more in a week.
options: A. Worker One on both measures
B. Worker One on the hourly rate; Worker Two on weekly pay
C. Worker Two on both measures
D. The two earn the same on both measures
E. Worker Two on the hourly rate; Worker One on weekly pay
questions.explanation: Hourly rates are given: Worker One GBP 18.40, Worker Two GBP 14.90. Weekly pay is rate multiplied by hours: Worker One GBP 404.80 and Worker Two GBP 566.20. The better-paid hour is worked far fewer times, so the higher rate does not produce the higher pay packet.

questions.prompt:
100 items are divided between three departments in the ratio 5 : 4 : 3, in whole items only, and whatever cannot be divided is kept back.

Select the largest department's share AND the number kept back.
options: A. 41 items to the largest; 3 kept back
B. 40 items to the largest; nothing kept back
C. 36 items to the largest; 4 kept back
D. 40 items to the largest; 4 kept back
E. 50 items to the largest; 4 kept back
questions.explanation: The ratio has 12 parts, and 100 divided by 12 is 8.33 — so one part is 8 whole items. The three shares are 40, 32, 24, together 96, leaving 4 kept back. Rounding the part up instead of down would need 108 items, more than there are.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): incidents attended — Station P 2,480, Station Q 1,020, Station R 3,900

SOURCE 2 (table): appliances in service — Station P 8, Station Q 3, Station R 14

SOURCE 3 (memo): "The next appliance goes to the station attending the most incidents for each appliance it already has."

Which station receives it?
options: A. Station P
B. Station R
C. Station Q
D. The three stations are equal
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Incidents divided by appliances: Station P 310, Station Q 340, Station R 279. Station Q is highest and runs the smallest fleet. Station R attends the most incidents outright, 3,900, but has 14 appliances to spread them across.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (report): "The average selling price rose from GBP 42 to GBP 51."

SOURCE 2 (note): "No individual product's price changed at any point during the year."

SOURCE 3 (table): the premium range went from 12% to 46% of units sold.

Which statement is best supported?
options: A. The average rose because the mix shifted towards the premium range, not because anything became dearer
B. Every product became more expensive over the year
C. Customers paid about 21% more for the same goods
D. The premium range must have been discounted
E. The average selling price is unrelated to which products sell
questions.explanation: Source 2 rules out any price rise, so the only thing that changed is which products were being bought, and source 3 shows the premium range going from about an eighth of sales to almost half. An average over a changing mix moves even when every price in it stands still.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): day rate — Contractor A GBP 940.00, Contractor B GBP 1,180.00, Contractor C GBP 1,050.00

SOURCE 2 (table): quality rating out of 5 — Contractor A 3.6, Contractor B 4.4, Contractor C 4.1

SOURCE 3 (email): "Engage the cheapest contractor rated 4 or above. The job runs 30 days."

Which contractor should be engaged?
options: A. Contractor A
B. Contractor B
C. Contractor C
D. All three cost the same
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Contractor A has the lowest day rate but is rated 3.6, below the 4 the email requires. Of the two that qualify, Contractor B would cost GBP 35,400.00 over 30 days and Contractor C would cost GBP 31,500.00 over 30 days, so Contractor C is the choice. The rating decides who is eligible; only then does the day rate decide between them.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (report): "Complaints fell 22% after the new system went live."

SOURCE 2 (note): the complaints form moved to a page reachable only through the account settings menu.

SOURCE 3 (table): visits to the complaints page fell 61%.

Which of these is NOT supported by the sources?
options: A. Fewer people reached the complaints form than before
B. Service quality improved by 22%
C. The fall in complaints coincided with the form becoming harder to find
D. Page visits fell by more, in percentage terms, than complaints did
E. The sources do not establish why complaints fell
questions.explanation: Sources 2 and 3 give a straightforward alternative explanation: the form got harder to reach and visits fell 61%, well beyond the 22% fall in complaints. Nothing in the three sources measures service quality at all, so reading the fall as a quality improvement is the one claim they will not carry. The other four are read directly off the sources.

questions.prompt:
What is the value of y?

(1) 5y = 45
(2) y divided by 3 equals 3
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) gives y = 45 / 5 = 9. (2) gives y = 3 × 3 = 9. Each statement alone pins the same value, and the two agree, so either is sufficient by itself.

questions.prompt:
A quadrilateral is known to be a rectangle. Is it a square?

(1) Its diagonals meet at right angles.
(2) Its diagonals are equal in length.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: A rectangle whose diagonals are perpendicular must have equal sides, so (1) settles the question with a yes. (2) is true of every rectangle without exception, so it distinguishes nothing and leaves the answer open.

questions.prompt:
What is the median of five numbers?

(1) Their mean is 20.
(2) The largest of them is 30.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: The set 10, 10, 20, 30, 30 has a mean of 20, a largest value of 30 and a median of 20. The set 0, 10, 30, 30, 30 has the same mean and the same largest value but a median of 30. Both satisfy the statements together, so even combined they leave the median open.

questions.prompt:
What is the capacity of a tank?

(1) Adding 30 litres would leave it three quarters full.
(2) It is currently half full and holds 60 litres.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) gives a relationship but no starting level, so the capacity could be almost anything. (2) says half the capacity is 60 litres, making the capacity 120 litres. The two are consistent: 60 plus 30 is 90, which is indeed three quarters of 120.

questions.prompt:
Which centre handles the most tonnes for each member of staff?

Centre | Staff | Tonnes received | Contamination rate | Open days a year
Alderney | 11 | 8,400 | 6.5% | 310
Belforth | 9 | 5,100 | 11.2% | 260
Carnwath | 22 | 15,600 | 4.2% | 340
Denmoor | 9 | 6,900 | 8.4% | 290
Eastwick | 17 | 11,200 | 5.2% | 330
Fallowby | 7 | 3,600 | 13.6% | 240
options: A. Alderney
B. Belforth
C. Denmoor
D. Carnwath
E. Eastwick
questions.explanation: Tonnes divided by staff: Alderney 764, Belforth 567, Carnwath 709, Denmoor 767, Eastwick 659, Fallowby 514. Denmoor is highest at about 767 tonnes a head. Carnwath takes in 15,600 tonnes, more than twice as much, but employs 22 people to do it.

questions.prompt:
Which centre receives the most contaminated tonnage in a year?

Centre | Staff | Tonnes received | Contamination rate | Open days a year
Alderney | 11 | 8,400 | 6.5% | 310
Belforth | 9 | 5,100 | 11.2% | 260
Carnwath | 22 | 15,600 | 4.2% | 340
Denmoor | 9 | 6,900 | 8.4% | 290
Eastwick | 17 | 11,200 | 5.2% | 330
Fallowby | 7 | 3,600 | 13.6% | 240
options: A. Alderney
B. Denmoor
C. Eastwick
D. Carnwath
E. Fallowby
questions.explanation: Contaminated tonnage is tonnes multiplied by the rate: Alderney 546, Belforth 571, Carnwath 655, Denmoor 580, Eastwick 582, Fallowby 490. Carnwath is highest — and it has the cleanest intake in the table at 4.2%. Fallowby has the worst rate at 13.6% but receives the least tonnage, so the rate alone points the wrong way.

questions.prompt:
How many centres receive more than 8,000 tonnes a year?

Centre | Staff | Tonnes received | Contamination rate | Open days a year
Alderney | 11 | 8,400 | 6.5% | 310
Belforth | 9 | 5,100 | 11.2% | 260
Carnwath | 22 | 15,600 | 4.2% | 340
Denmoor | 9 | 6,900 | 8.4% | 290
Eastwick | 17 | 11,200 | 5.2% | 330
Fallowby | 7 | 3,600 | 13.6% | 240
options: A. Three
B. One
C. Two
D. Four
E. Five
questions.explanation: Tonnes received: Alderney 8,400, Belforth 5,100, Carnwath 15,600, Denmoor 6,900, Eastwick 11,200, Fallowby 3,600. Above 8,000: Alderney, Carnwath, Eastwick — 3 centres. Denmoor is the nearest below the line at 6,900 tonnes.

questions.prompt:
How many centres are above the median on tonnes per member of staff and below the median on contamination rate?

Centre | Staff | Tonnes received | Contamination rate | Open days a year
Alderney | 11 | 8,400 | 6.5% | 310
Belforth | 9 | 5,100 | 11.2% | 260
Carnwath | 22 | 15,600 | 4.2% | 340
Denmoor | 9 | 6,900 | 8.4% | 290
Eastwick | 17 | 11,200 | 5.2% | 330
Fallowby | 7 | 3,600 | 13.6% | 240
options: A. One
B. Three
C. Four
D. Five
E. Two
questions.explanation: The medians are 684 tonnes a head and 7.45% contamination. Above on tonnes per head: Alderney, Carnwath, Denmoor. Below on contamination: Alderney, Carnwath, Eastwick. On both: Alderney and Carnwath — 2. Throughput per head and cleanliness of intake overlap here, but they are not the same ranking.
